title: Sign off on a visit with Provider Attestation (step 17)

claims.claim: Step 17 of the Visit Wizard is where you attest and sign and record E/M time; you then review remaining gaps, preview the progress note, finish with Sign & Lock, and use an addendum for corrections after signing.
Step 16 is the LCD Navigator™ checklist.

checks.pattern: LCD Navigator dismissed — reopen by clicking Step 16

claims.claim: Before you start: all 17 steps of the Visit Wizard are complete, and you have confirmed that all clinical documentation reflects the actual care provided during this encounter.
You are the rendering provider — a clinician with a provider profession title (NP, PA, MD, DO) or a medical director. Support staff cannot complete Provider Attestation.

checks.note: no role gate exists in the step
a provider-only step would not offer RN as a title

claims.finding: Step 17 has no role gate. The signer is the visit's clinician when they hold a valid 10-digit NPI, otherwise the supervising provider chosen in Step 2 (ProviderAttestationVisit.tsx:107-114, :403-419 at v1.1.345); the Professional Title list includes RN, LPN and LVN (:688-690). The only lock-out is view-only in completion mode (VisitWizardV4.tsx:18723).
claims.proposed_text: Step 17 is filled in for the visit's clinician when they have a valid 10-digit NPI. Otherwise the supervising provider chosen in Step 2 signs. If the wizard was opened in completion mode, Provider Attestation is view only.

claims.claim: Under CMS documentation requirements, the rendering provider — not a scribe or co-signing clinician alone — must attest to the accuracy and completeness of the encounter note. Verify your organization's co-signature policy before delegating attestation.
Open Step 17 — Provider Attestation in the Visit Wizard.
The provider information fills in automatically: full name and NPI.
Select your Professional Title.
Read the attestation statement, which confirms the documentation is accurate and complete.

checks.pattern: I attest that this documentation is accurate, complete, and
compliant with LCD and payer documentation requirements.

claims.claim: Check the Provider Attestation Acknowledgment box.
claims.finding: The checkbox is labelled 'Provider Attestation', with the statement under it (ProviderAttestationVisit.tsx:743-768 at v1.1.345). No 'Provider Attestation Acknowledgment' label exists.

claims.claim: Select the electronic signature option to sign.

checks.note: a selectable signature option would have to exist

claims.finding: There is no signature option to select and nothing to draw. The electronic signature is the typed line 'Electronically Signed By: name, title, NPI, date', made when you tick Provider Attestation and click Complete Provider Attestation (ProviderAttestationVisit.tsx:311-315, :781-790, :818 at v1.1.345).
claims.proposed_text: Check the Electronic Signature Preview. Your electronic signature is the typed line "Electronically Signed By:" with your name, title, NPI and the date. It is recorded when you click Complete Provider Attestation.

claims.claim: Your electronic signature is your attestation that the assessment, treatments, procedures, and findings in the note reflect the care you provided.
If you are choosing the E/M level by total time rather than medical decision-making, enter Total E/M Time (Minutes): the time you spent on the date of service.

checks.pattern: Optional. Total time you spent on the date of service, not counting time spent on
separately billed procedures. Leave blank to bill by medical decision-making. This

claims.claim: Qualifying E/M time can include reviewing records, evaluating the patient and wound, educating the patient or caregiver, coordinating care, planning treatment, and documenting.
Exclude time spent performing separately billed procedures.

checks.pattern: Optional. Total time you spent on the date of service, not counting time spent on
separately billed procedures. Leave blank to bill by medical decision-making. This

claims.claim: Entering time supports time-based coding; it does not by itself make an E/M service separately billable.
Confirm your professional title, signature, acknowledgment, and E/M time.
Click Complete Provider Attestation.
Click Mark as Complete. Step 17 shows as completed.
In the section navigator, check that every section that applies is marked complete.
claims.finding: There is no section navigator. Each section's header in the wizard shows a status icon; complete sections show a green check (VisitWizardV4.tsx:11261-11273 at v1.1.345).
claims.proposed_text: Scroll the wizard and check that every section that applies shows a green checkmark in its header.

proposed_checks.pattern: const StatusIcon: React.FC<{ sectionId: string }> = ({ sectionId }) => {

claims.claim: Click Continue Review. Medipyxis checks the documentation and lists any remaining gaps in a window. For each gap choose Resolve This (go to the section, fix it, then Continue Review again) or Continue Anyway.
claims.finding: The button is 'Continue to Review' at the bottom of the wizard (VisitWizardV4.tsx:19062-19086 at v1.1.345). If gaps remain it opens 'Documentation gaps' (DocumentationAssistModal.tsx:536). Each gap has its own Go to <section> / Answer / Skip actions; the window's buttons are 'Resolve' (closes it so you can fix things) and 'Continue anyway' (:740-743). No 'Resolve This' or 'Continue Anyway' (capital A) exists.
claims.proposed_text: Click Continue to Review at the bottom of the wizard. If documentation gaps remain, a Documentation gaps window lists them. Use each item's button to go to the section and fix it, or answer it in the box. Click Resolve to close the window and keep working, then click Continue to Review again. Or click Continue anyway to go on.

claims.claim: Continue Anyway does not make the documentation meet medical necessity, billing, or LCD requirements; you decide whether a gap must be fixed before signing.

checks.pattern: I understand this claim is missing {billingGapNames} and I am continuing anyway

claims.reason: Product side: continuing is the clinician's decision and, for billing-affecting gaps, records an acknowledgment. The label case ('Continue anyway') is covered by so-21.

claims.claim: The Wound Care Progress Note Preview shows the note as a PDF.
claims.finding: The preview screen is headed 'Preview — Review Before Signing' (ProgressNotePreview.tsx:92 at v1.1.345). No 'Wound Care Progress Note Preview' title exists.
claims.proposed_text: The Preview — Review Before Signing screen shows the note as a PDF, exactly as it will be finalized.

claims.claim: The preview is the note exactly as it will be finalized: patient and encounter details, chief complaint and history, review of systems and objective assessment, wound findings and measurements, previous treatments and medical necessity, interventions and procedure notes, the treatment plan, education and medications, billing documentation, and your attestation.

checks.pattern: // Copied before openSignReview clears the React blob. Sign files this copy.

claims.claim: If anything needs correcting, go back to that section before you sign.
Click Continue, review the final signing options, then click Sign & Lock.

checks.note: the preview's button would have to read Continue

claims.finding: The preview's button reads 'Looks Good, Continue →' (ProgressNotePreview.tsx:155 at v1.1.345). It opens the review window (Visit Time, Review Notes, Cancel Review), whose button is Sign & Lock (MultiWoundReviewModal.tsx:846-1042). If the service date differs from the appointment date, a Date check prompt appears first.
claims.proposed_text: Click Looks Good, Continue →. In the review window, check the visit time and review notes, then click Sign & Lock.

claims.claim: The signed note becomes the finalized clinical record for the visit; the note is signed and locked.

checks.pattern: export const SIGNED_AND_LOCKED_TITLE = "This visit is signed and locked";

claims.claim: Medipyxis generates the finalized wound care progress note PDF and saves it to the patient's record — open the patient's chart, go to Progress Notes, and open the visit to view it.

checks.pattern: The PDF stays in pendingChartNoteRef until Sign & Lock.

claims.claim: The visit's billing information goes to Billing Operations as a pre-filled CMS-1500 claim for your biller to review.
If your facility uses a co-signature workflow, the note may enter a Pending Co-Signature state; the supervising provider receives an in-app notification and must also complete their attestation step.
claims.finding: There is no Pending Co-Signature state or co-sign notification. Co-signature is the optional Physician Sign-Off section, which shows 'Co-sign Requested' when the appointment is flagged and never blocks save or sign (VisitWizardV4.tsx:18742-18792 at v1.1.345).
claims.proposed_text: If your practice uses co-signature, the supervising clinician completes the optional Physician Sign-Off section. When the appointment was flagged for co-signature, the section shows Co-sign Requested. It does not block saving or Sign & Lock.

claims.claim: Once a note is signed, the encounter is read-only; to correct or add information, use the addendum process.

checks.pattern: export const SIGNED_AND_LOCKED_TITLE = "This visit is signed and locked";

claims.claim: Open the locked encounter from the patient chart or Fleet Calendar.
Click Addendum in the top action bar.
claims.finding: Opening a signed visit shows the 'This visit is signed and locked' screen with an 'Add an addendum' button (SignedVisitScreen.tsx, AddAddendumToNoteButton.tsx at v1.1.345); it opens the 'Add Addendum to Progress Note' form. There is no 'Addendum' button in a top action bar.
claims.proposed_text: On the "This visit is signed and locked" screen, click Add an addendum.

claims.claim: Select an addendum reason from the dropdown. The list covers three kinds of correction: clinical corrections (a correction to clinical documentation, or additional findings documented after the visit), billing corrections (a billing code correction), and corrections to written-in language.
claims.finding: The dropdown is 'Type of Addendum' with Correction, Clarification, Late entry, Fabrication remediation and Other (NATURE_OF_AMENDMENT_OPTIONS, WoundDetailPage.tsx:211-219 at v1.1.345). The reason is free text of at least 10 characters. Sentence-kind items are checkboxes under 'Fabricated Statements to Remediate', shown only for Fabrication remediation.
claims.proposed_text: Pick the Type of Addendum: Correction, Clarification, Late entry, Fabrication remediation, or Other. Write the reason (at least 10 characters). For a sentence in a signed note that you did not write, choose Fabrication remediation and tick the kind of sentence.

claims.claim: Corrections to written-in language name a specific kind of sentence, for example Procedure tolerance was a template default or LCD citation was wrong (cited policy does not govern this service).

checks.pattern: label: "Procedure tolerance was a template default",
label: "LCD citation was wrong (cited policy does not govern this service)",

claims.claim: A reviewer reads the reason alongside the addendum text.
Pick the reason that names what you are correcting; a precise reason is worth more than a general one. Describe what changed and why, and do not delete or re-state the original note.
The addendum appears as a dated attachment below the original signed note.

checks.pattern: Appended to the signed note above (filed ${filedAt}). Original note unaltered above.

claims.claim: Click Save Addendum.
claims.finding: The button is labelled 'Submit Addendum' (WoundDetailPage.tsx at v1.1.345).

claims.claim: The addendum is appended to the encounter record with your name, credential, and a new timestamp.
Addendum content is permanently appended to the encounter record.
Addendum content is visible in audit logs.
claims.finding: No audit-log view reads progress_note_addendums, and create-progress-note-addendum writes no audit row (its 'audit trail' is the provider_name on the addendum itself, handler.ts:359 at v1.1.345). Addenda are visible on the note itself (renderAddenda) and are append-only.
claims.proposed_text: Addendum content is permanently appended to the encounter record and prints on the note under the original.

claims.claim: Do not use the addendum to alter the clinical meaning of a note after the fact without a legitimate clinical or administrative reason.
Troubleshooting: Complete Provider Attestation doesn't finish the step because the professional title, acknowledgment, or signature is missing — select your title, check the acknowledgment, and sign.

checks.note: the button would have to wait for a signature input

claims.finding: Complete Provider Attestation stays disabled until the provider name, Professional Title, a 10-digit NPI and the Provider Attestation tick are all present (ProviderAttestationVisit.tsx:800-807 at v1.1.345). There is no separate signature to give; the signature line is made by the button itself.
claims.proposed_text: Complete Provider Attestation is greyed out: the provider name, Professional Title, 10-digit NPI or the Provider Attestation tick is missing. Fill them in and tick the box.

claims.claim: Troubleshooting: a window lists documentation gaps after Continue Review — click Resolve This for each, or Continue Anyway.
claims.finding: Same labels as so-21: the button is Continue to Review, and the gaps window's buttons are Resolve and Continue anyway (DocumentationAssistModal.tsx:740-743 at v1.1.345).
claims.proposed_text: A Documentation gaps window opens after Continue to Review: some sections still have missing items. Fix them from each item's button, or click Continue anyway if you have decided they don't prevent finalizing.

claims.claim: Troubleshooting: Provider Attestation step is not accessible because your account is not a rendering provider — ask the rendering provider to sign in and complete step 17.
claims.finding: Step 17 is not gated by account role; it is view only only when the wizard runs in completion mode (VisitWizardV4.tsx:18723, ProviderAttestationVisit.tsx 'Provider authored · view only' at v1.1.345).
claims.proposed_text: Provider Attestation shows "Provider authored · view only": the wizard was opened in completion mode. Ask the provider to open the visit and complete step 17.

claims.claim: Troubleshooting: the appointment still shows Draft Saved after signing — refresh the Fleet Calendar.
claims.reason: Code shows the status names and that signing sets Visit Completed; the stale-browser cause cannot be shown from code.

claims.claim: Troubleshooting: the addendum reason dropdown is empty because your organization has not configured addendum reasons — contact your administrator to configure addendum reason codes.
claims.finding: The Type of Addendum options are hard-coded and the same for every organization (NATURE_OF_AMENDMENT_OPTIONS, WoundDetailPage.tsx:211 at v1.1.345). There is nothing to configure, so the list cannot be empty for this reason.
claims.proposed_text: Delete this row. The Type of Addendum list is built in and the same for every organization.

claims.claim: Troubleshooting: the Addendum button is not visible because the note is not yet signed (still in draft) — complete Provider Attestation first.

checks.note: the signed screen would have to open once step 17 is attested

claims.finding: The signed screen with Add an addendum appears only for a visit that went through Sign & Lock (visit_locked; resolveWizardArrival.ts decideWizardEntry, visitSignState.ts 'Signed means Sign & Lock ran' at v1.1.345). Completing Provider Attestation alone does not sign the visit — step 17 itself says 'Not signed yet — Sign & Lock finishes it'.
claims.proposed_text: There is no Add an addendum button: the visit has not been through Sign & Lock. Finish it with Continue to Review and Sign & Lock.

proposed_checks.pattern: Not signed yet — Sign & Lock finishes it
